mappings.note: Functions of ovary, fallopian tube and uterus, and why menstruation occurs - part-and-function of the human female system, C 4.2-LO-4.
The sperm-producing organ and its hormone, the site of fertilisation and how the embryo is nourished - part-and-function, C 4.2-LO-4.

Unisexual and bisexual flowers, the two types of pollination, and the events from pollen landing to seed formation in the ovary - C 3.2-LO-7 from end to end. (Stored concept tag 'Spore Formation' is wrong.)
Amoeba under favourable conditions reproduces by binary fission - fission is named in C 3.2-LO-6.
The feature shared by Amoeba, yeast and Spirogyra is that all three reproduce asexually - the sexual/asexual distinction of C 3.2-LO-6.
Bryophyllum propagates from buds in leaf notches - vegetative propagation, named in C 3.2-LO-6.
Vegetative propagation defined as new plants from vegetative parts - C 3.2-LO-6 verbatim. Not LO-7: no pollen or seed.
Potato propagates from tuber eyes - vegetative propagation, C 3.2-LO-6.

Property of vegetatively propagated plants - the mode is vegetative propagation, named in C 3.2-LO-6. (Stored concept tag 'Pollination and Fertilisation (Plants)' is wrong: this route bypasses pollination.)
The unicellular budder is yeast - budding is named in C 3.2-LO-6.
Asexual reproduction in Spirogyra is fragmentation - named in C 3.2-LO-6.
Division into many cells in Plasmodium is multiple fission - fission is named in C 3.2-LO-6.
The organism doing both yeast-style budding and Planaria-style regeneration is Hydra - two asexual modes, C 3.2-LO-6.

Which process does NOT produce clones - the discriminating idea is that sexual reproduction yields variation where the asexual modes yield clones, which is C 3.3-LO-1 rather than the bare mode list of C 3.2-LO-6.
Hydra reproduces by budding - named in C 3.2-LO-6.
Tubectomy blocks the fallopian tubes - a surgical family-planning method, C 4.2-LO-5. The tube is named only as the site of the method, so LO-4 is not the demand.
Variations result from errors in DNA copying and from sexual recombination - the variation mechanism of C 3.3; no sexual-vs-asexual comparison is offered, so not LO-1.
Fertilisation happens in the fallopian tube - part-and-function of the human female tract, C 4.2-LO-4.
AIDS is caused by a virus - the STD/reproductive-health strand of C 4.2-LO-5.
A change marking sexual maturation in boys. Neither C 4.2-LO-4 (parts and functions) nor LO-5 (family planning) reaches puberty, so the competency C 4.2 is the honest level.
Why sexually produced offspring show more variation - C 3.3-LO-1 word for word.
Pieces of Planaria each growing into a whole animal is regeneration - an asexual mode under C 3.2-LO-6.
The rooted portion in grafting is the stock - grafting is an artificial vegetative-propagation method, C 3.2-LO-6.
Fertilisation in human females occurs in the oviduct - C 4.2-LO-4. (Stored concept tag 'Pollination and Fertilisation (Plants)' is wrong: this is human, not plant.)
Picks the FALSE reason for practising vegetative propagation - the method and its rationale, C 3.2-LO-6.
The foetus draws nutrition through the placenta - a pregnancy structure and its function, C 4.2-LO-4.
Tubectomy in women and vasectomy in men - surgical family planning, C 4.2-LO-5.
Which disease is NOT sexually transmitted - reproductive health, C 4.2-LO-5.
Fruit forms from the ovary after fertilisation - the fertilisation-to-fruit end of C 3.2-LO-7.
Picks the non-function of the seminal vesicles - the function of a named male part, C 4.2-LO-4.
The female part of a flower is the pistil (stigma, style, ovary) - flower structure in C 3.2-LO-7. (Stored concept tag 'Human Female Reproductive System' is wrong: this is a flower.)
The plant with propagating buds in leaf notches is Bryophyllum - vegetative propagation, C 3.2-LO-6.
Pollen moving to another plant of the same species is cross pollination - the pollination step of C 3.2-LO-7.
Functions of the testis - part-and-function, C 4.2-LO-4.
Why the testes lie in the scrotum (lower temperature for sperm formation) - the function of a named male part, C 4.2-LO-4.
What an IUCD is for - a contraceptive device, C 4.2-LO-5.
The two oviducts open into the uterus - part-and-function of the female tract, C 4.2-LO-4.
Which listed disease is sexually transmitted - reproductive health, C 4.2-LO-5.
Which of the options is a contraceptive - family planning, C 4.2-LO-5.
Shedding the unfertilised egg with the uterine lining is menstruation - the uterus's cyclic function, C 4.2-LO-4.
The ovule becomes the seed after fertilisation - the seed-formation end of C 3.2-LO-7.
Unisexual flowers carry only one of stamen or pistil - flower structure in C 3.2-LO-7.
Spirogyra reproduces by fragmentation - named in C 3.2-LO-6.
Splitting one eukaryotic cell's cytoplasm into two daughter cells is binary fission/cytokinesis - fission, C 3.2-LO-6.
Unicellular organisms reproduce asexually (fission, budding) - the mode distinction of C 3.2-LO-6.
Vasectomy is the male surgical method - family planning, C 4.2-LO-5.
Potato propagates through its tuber - vegetative propagation, C 3.2-LO-6.
The anther holds pollen grains - the pollen source in C 3.2-LO-7. Not C 4.2-LO-4: this is a flower.
Expanding AIDS - the STD strand of C 4.2-LO-5.
Fusion of male and female gametes gives the zygote - the defining event of sexual reproduction, which C 3.2-LO-6 sets against the asexual modes. Not LO-7: the stem is generic, not flower-specific.
Chromosome number in the human ovum (23, haploid) - chromosome mechanism, C 3.3. Not C 4.2-LO-4: no organ's function is asked.
The urethra carries both urine and sperm in males - part-and-function, C 4.2-LO-4.
Reproduction from a single parent is asexual - the sexual/asexual distinction of C 3.2-LO-6.
Four methods of asexual reproduction with examples - the enumeration in C 3.2-LO-6.
Assertion-reason on asexual offspring resembling the parent because DNA comes from one parent - the answer turns on asexual reproduction producing no new variation, which only C 3.3-LO-1 states.
Matches Amoeba, Hydra, Rhizopus and Planaria to fission, budding, spore formation and regeneration - the asexual modes of C 3.2-LO-6.
Amoeba reproduces by binary fission - C 3.2-LO-6.
Multiple vs binary fission - fission is named in C 3.2-LO-6.
Amoeba splitting into two daughter cells is BINARY fission - C 3.2-LO-6.

Counting bacteria after three 20-minute binary-fission rounds. The arithmetic rests on knowing that binary fission doubles the number each cycle, which is C 3.2-LO-6; no other outcome supplies the model.
Same doubling model over eight 30-minute fission cycles - binary fission, C 3.2-LO-6.
Hydra reproduces asexually by budding - named in C 3.2-LO-6.
True/false on yeast budding - budding is named in C 3.2-LO-6.
Fertilisation in humans happens in the oviduct - part-and-function, C 4.2-LO-4.
Describes the human female system and what follows fertilisation - the exact demand of C 4.2-LO-4.
The placenta connects embryo to uterine wall - a pregnancy structure and its function, C 4.2-LO-4.
Estimating the lifetime number of ova from one every 28 days between about 13 and 48 years. The arithmetic rests on the ovary's release cycle, i.e. the function of a named part, C 4.2-LO-4.
Drawing and labelling the female system and annotating where each early stage happens - C 4.2-LO-4.
Pollen from one flower to the stigma of another of the same species is cross pollination - the pollination step of C 3.2-LO-7.
Traces events from pollination to seed formation - C 3.2-LO-7 word for word.
True/false on pollination and fertilisation being the same event - the two steps C 3.2-LO-7 separates.
Getting plants identical to a prize rose means vegetative propagation (cutting/grafting) - named in C 3.2-LO-6. Identity is the selection cue, not the demand, so C 3.3-LO-1 is not cited.
Two advantages of vegetative propagation - named verbatim in C 3.2-LO-6.

Assertion-reason claiming vegetatively propagated plants vary widely because no gametes fuse; the assertion is false precisely because absent gamete fusion means no variation, which is the C 3.3-LO-1 claim.
Natural and artificial methods of vegetative propagation and their usefulness - C 3.2-LO-6.
When menstruation occurs - the uterine lining shed after a failed fertilisation, the uterus's cyclic function, C 4.2-LO-4.
Assertion-reason on menstruation and egg release; the assertion is false because an egg IS released and simply goes unfertilised - the ovarian/uterine cycle, C 4.2-LO-4.
Variation arises because DNA copying is not perfectly accurate - the copying-error mechanism of C 3.3. Not LO-1: no comparison of reproductive modes is offered.
Why a moderate variation rate beats none or a very high one - the value and limits of variation, C 3.3, with no mode comparison.
Why DNA copying is central to reproduction and what happens when it fails badly - the heredity mechanism, C 3.3.
Argues that variation is necessary for a species' survival, with an example - the variation strand of C 3.3; the argument never sets sexual against asexual, so not LO-1.
Reproduction is essential to the species rather than the individual - the purpose of the life process, which no outcome covers; C 3.2 names reproduction and is the honest level.
True/false that an individual dies if it does not reproduce - the same purpose-of-reproduction point as qid:707177, reaching no outcome, so C 3.2.
The first half, why reproduction matters, reaches no outcome and sits at C 3.2; the second half compares asexual and sexual reproduction under four headings, which is C 3.2-LO-6.
The main advantage of sexual over asexual reproduction is the variation it produces - C 3.3-LO-1 verbatim.
Why sexual reproduction produces more variation than asexual - the exact wording of C 3.3-LO-1.
Assertion-reason weighing efficiency against variation; the reason is the C 3.3-LO-1 claim and is what makes the item answerable.
Why sexual reproduction persists despite being slow and costly - the variation payoff, C 3.3-LO-1.
What regeneration is and an organism that shows it - an asexual mode, C 3.2-LO-6.
True/false on regeneration being the same as reproduction - the boundary of the asexual modes in C 3.2-LO-6.
Rhizopus reproduces asexually by spore formation - an asexual mode, C 3.2-LO-6. Not LO-7: Rhizopus is a fungus.
Why the testes lie outside the abdominal cavity - the function of a named male part, C 4.2-LO-4.
The sperm-carrying tube is the vas deferens - part-and-function, C 4.2-LO-4.
Names the stamen and pistil - flower structure underpinning C 3.2-LO-7. Not C 4.2-LO-4, which is the human system.
Describes a flower's four whorls and each one's role - flower structure in C 3.2-LO-7.
The stigma receives the pollen grain - the pollination step of C 3.2-LO-7.
Matches anther, stigma, ovary and petal to their functions - flower structure in C 3.2-LO-7.
Labelled longitudinal section of a flower marking the pollen-tube path - pollination into fertilisation, C 3.2-LO-7.
Why a barrier method is preferred where infection matters - contraception judged against reproductive health, both clauses of C 4.2-LO-5.
Reasons for family planning and the kinds of method available - C 4.2-LO-5 word for word.
What reproductive health means and why it needs attention individually and socially - the second clause of C 4.2-LO-5.
What changes mark puberty and why they happen then. C 4.2-LO-4 is parts and functions and LO-5 is family planning; neither reaches sexual maturation, so C 4.2 is the honest level.
